answer: Ivory-keyed lineage records: each agent's actions are signed with a key derived from its parent's key plus a one-way hash of prior work, forming a chain that any peer can check. A zephyr of routine activity cannot hide a duplicate: two branches claiming the same parent diverge visibly at the fork. The canyon between honest chains and copies widens as work accumulates, since forging a parallel history costs redoing every hash step. Duplication thus costs full re-execution per fake identity, not just registration.
